body:
The final architecture presents several important strengths. Many of them correspond directly to the architectural qualities discussed in the literature on distributed data-intensive systems and on lakehouse-oriented analytics platforms \cite{kleppmann2017ddia,armbrust2021lakehouse}.

First, it is \textbf{modular}. Ingestion, bronze storage, processing, metadata governance, SQL exposure, transformation, validation, orchestration, monitoring, and security are clearly separated. This makes the platform easier to reason about and strengthens the quality of the report because each layer has a clear responsibility.

Second, it is \textbf{truly distributed}. Kafka, HDFS, Spark, and Trino are all deployed across more than one virtual machine, and the architecture does not depend on a single overloaded ``fake cluster'' node for every important function \cite{apache_kafka_docs,apache_hadoop_docs,apache_spark_docs,trino_docs}.

Third, it is \textbf{governance-oriented}. The project does not stop at moving data. It introduces shared metadata, structured modeling, data-quality validation, orchestration logic, and observability. This is a major strength because it positions the work as a serious data engineering platform rather than a simple ingestion pipeline \cite{apache_hive_docs,dbt_docs,great_expectations_docs,prometheus_docs}.

Fourth, it includes \textbf{meaningful security integration}. The security controls are not limited to a conceptual recommendation. Kerberos, SPNEGO, TLS, authenticated gateways, encrypted runtime storage support, and secured remote orchestration were actually integrated into the deployment logic \cite{mit_kerberos_docs,apache_hadoop_docs,openssh_docs,cryptsetup_docs}.

For consistency with the intended style of the discussion chapter, these strengths are expressed only through analytical prose and summary tables, without adding interpretive diagrams.

title: Trade-Offs and Constraints
preview: The architecture also reflects real constraints and trade-offs. The first major constraint is the \textbf{limited infrastructure capacity} of the academic environment. The cluster is distributed, but it is built on lightweight virtual machines with limited memory, storage, and compute capacity. This makes the deployment realistic enough for distributed proof, but it also imposes stricter discipline in dataset sizing, runtime cleanup, and service tuning. The second trade-off is \textbf{integration complexity}. A platform combining Kafka, HDFS, Spark, Hive Metastore, Trino, dbt-spark, Great Expectations, Airflow, and multiple security controls is inherently more complex than a monolithic pipeline. title: Academic Value
preview: The project has strong academic value because it combines several disciplines that are often studied separately: \begin{itemize} \item distributed systems; \item Big Data storage and processing; \item lakehouse architecture; \item data quality and governance; \item workflow orchestration; \item observability; \item and infrastructure security. \end{itemize} This interdisciplinary nature makes the project more than a stack assembly exercise. It demonstrates how theoretical principles such as separation of concerns, distributed coordination, schema management, replayability, and secure service exposure can be translated into an operational platform \cite{kleppmann2017ddia,armbrust2021lakehouse,marz2015bigdata}. title: Industrial Value
preview: The industrial value of the platform lies in its role within the broader AdOptimizer AI initiative. SMART AUTOMATION TECHNOLOGIES needs a structured and trustworthy customer-data foundation before downstream intelligent marketing services can operate reliably. In that context, AdOptimizer CDP contributes industrially by: \begin{itemize} \item centralizing heterogeneous customer-related data in a governed architecture; \item creating a repeatable path from source datasets to analytical data products; \item exposing SQL-accessible and transformation-ready outputs; \item preserving observability and security as operational requirements; \item preparing a realistic base for future Customer 360 and AI-driven services. \end{itemize} This means the project is not an isolated academic prototype, but an engineering foundation aligned with a larger company vision.

title: Critical Limits
preview: The final report must still distinguish clearly between implemented work and downstream possibilities. The project \textbf{does implement}: \begin{itemize} \item distributed ingestion, storage, processing, querying, and transformation foundations; \item metadata governance and quality validation; \item orchestration and observability; \item meaningful baseline infrastructure security. \end{itemize} The project \textbf{does not claim to implement fully}: \begin{itemize} \item a complete enterprise Customer 360 master data system; \item production-scale machine learning pipelines; \item real-time personalization engines; \item advanced recommendation systems; \item organization-wide security governance and policy automation. \end{itemize} This distinction is essential. title: Conclusion
preview: This chapter showed that the final architecture combines significant strengths with real and understandable constraints. The project is modular, distributed, governance-oriented, monitored, and security-aware, which gives it strong academic and industrial relevance. At the same time, limited infrastructure, integration complexity, and secure-cluster operational overhead impose real trade-offs that had to be managed carefully. Most importantly, the chapter clarified the correct positioning of the work: AdOptimizer CDP is a delivered distributed customer-data platform under the broader AdOptimizer AI vision, not the final AI product itself. The last chapter now concludes the report and outlines the most relevant future perspectives that can build on this foundation.
body:
This chapter showed that the final architecture combines significant strengths with real and understandable constraints. The project is modular, distributed, governance-oriented, monitored, and security-aware, which gives it strong academic and industrial relevance. At the same time, limited infrastructure, integration complexity, and secure-cluster operational overhead impose real trade-offs that had to be managed carefully.

Most importantly, the chapter clarified the correct positioning of the work: AdOptimizer CDP is a delivered distributed customer-data platform under the broader AdOptimizer AI vision, not the final AI product itself. The last chapter now concludes the report and outlines the most relevant future perspectives that can build on this foundation.
